claims.text: The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs nanoparticles are uniformly mixed solid solutions.
A controlled thermal or chemical treatment can induce Ru segregation to the nanoparticle surface.
The treatment increases the local surface concentration of Ru relative to the bulk.
Surface enrichment of Ru shifts or otherwise modifies the catalyst's local d-band electronic structure.
Modification of the local electronic structure tunes the adsorption energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Ru enrichment modifies the electronic properties of active sites adjacent to surface Ru.
The electronic modification tunes the binding of acetaldehyde and acetate intermediates.
Tuned intermediate binding facilitates more efficient ethanol-oxidation pathways.
Tuned intermediate binding reduces poisoning caused by overly strong adsorption of reaction intermediates.
Ru-enriched PtPdRhRuIrOs catalysts will have higher ethanol-oxidation selectivity than catalysts with a uniform elemental distribution.
Ru-enriched catalysts will show greater turnover toward desired oxidation products.
Ru-enriched catalysts will accumulate fewer poisoning intermediates than the baseline catalysts.
Catalysts synthesized without surface-enrichment treatment retain a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The proposed mechanism should operate under standard acidic or alkaline ethanol-oxidation conditions at ambient to moderate temperatures.
Extreme pH, temperature, or potential may cause degradation or phase separation that invalidates the proposed mechanism.
Operando or in-situ X-ray absorption spectroscopy can help assess treatment-induced electronic-structure changes and intermediate adsorption.
Ru surface enrichment may cause long-term structural instability.
Interactions with the other platinum-group elements may counterbalance the expected electronic modulation from Ru enrichment.
